tool.name: MIC-50-90 laboratory report
tool.description: choose the counts that let readers check stated answers
tool.command: ln -s '$counts' counts.csv && ln -s '$panels' panels.csv && ln -s '$targets' targets.csv && #if $queries: ln -s '$queries' queries.csv && #end if mic-50-90 reporting-audit counts.csv --panels panels.csv --targets targets.csv --reporting-plan #if $queries: --decision-queries queries.csv #end if --decision-plan-time-limit $time_limit --report-page-size 0 --delimiter comma $fail_on_refusal --output-dir out

param.name: counts
param.label: Complete category counts
param.help: One row per cohort and category, zeros included: category, count, cohort_id, panel_id, rank_convention, iid, confidence_level (examples/appendix/inputs/laboratory in the MIC-50-90 repository).

param.name: panels
param.label: Category table
param.help: Explicit categories: panel_id, unit, category, panel_value, lower, upper, lower_closed, upper_closed.

param.name: targets
param.label: Questions for the readers
param.help: One row per question: cohort_id, threshold, unit, decision_operator, decision_fraction (for example < and 0.05 for 'fewer than 5% above the threshold').

param.name: queries
param.label: Counts the laboratory may publish, with their cost (optional)
param.help: cohort_id, threshold, unit, cost. Without this table every count above a category boundary may be published at cost 1.

param.name: time_limit
param.label: Seconds per cohort for the search

param.name: fail_on_refusal
param.label: Fail the job if any cohort is refused
param.help: Refused cohorts are always listed in the outputs with their reason.

tool.help:
**What it does**
A laboratory that holds the complete MIC category counts of a collection often publishes only MIC50, MIC90 and a few percentages. This tool finds the smallest set of additional counts the laboratory should publish so that readers can check each stated answer themselves, for example whether fewer than 5% of the isolates have an MIC above 4 mg/L.
Example: for 276 canine *E. coli* isolates tested with amikacin, MIC50 and MIC90 alone leave four questions about the share above 4, 8, 16 and 32 mg/L open. Publishing one count, 8 isolates above 4 mg/L, settles all four, because every isolate above a higher threshold is also above 4 mg/L.
**Inputs**
- *Complete category counts*: every recorded category with its count, zeros included; the counts must add up to the number of isolates. - *Category table*: the declared measurement categories and their open or closed ends. - *Questions for the readers*: a threshold and a criterion per question. - *Counts the laboratory may publish* (optional): restricts the candidates and gives each a cost.
**Outputs**
- *counts to publish*: the selected counts. - *certificate for readers*: the file a reader checks with **MIC-50-90 check a received report**, without the complete counts. - *answers before and after*: each question with its bounds from the summaries alone and its answer. - *report*, *results (JSON)* and *reusable input*: the program's HTML report, full results and settings.
The answers concern the observed collection and assume that the published counts are true. A complete count table remains the best archive.
**More information**
Documentation: https://github.com/maciejkochanowski/mic-50-90/tree/main/docs
